clips.text: Let's go home to Jefferson Park. Bready Mercury has been alone all week.
clips.script: [warm, eager] Let's go home to Jefferson Park. [fretting, doting] Bready Mercury has been alone ALL week.

clips.text: Welcome home. Don't open the salad spinner. That's loaf thirty-one.
clips.script: [mellow, warm] welcome home. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, easy, matter-of-fact] don't open the salad spinner. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, relaxed] that's loaf thirty-one.

clips.text: Tata. Did you touch it?
clips.script: [sharp, intent] Tata. [serious, demanding] Did you TOUCH it?

clips.text: Shut that door. You're letting the cold in.
clips.script: [gruff, cold, old workman] Shut that door. [grumbling] You're letting the cold in.

clips.text: 8:42 this morning. White sedan, parked across the Washington driveway for four minutes. Rental. Airport lot sticker on the windshield. I have the plate.
clips.script: [crisp, reporting] Eight forty-two this morning. White sedan, parked across the Washington driveway for four minutes. [dry, precise] Rental. Airport lot sticker on the windshield. [satisfied, flat] I have the PLATE.

clips.text: The drawer is ready for number eight. Also, a fancy letter came for you from the Moon Club. That place has been locked since 1971. I did not open it.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, brisk] The drawer is ready for number eight. [warm Long Island accent, curious] Also, a fancy letter came for you from the Moon Club. [warm Long Island accent, firm] That place has been locked since nineteen seventy-one. [warm Long Island accent, proud] I did not OPEN it.

clips.text: BOO!
clips.script: [gleeful, shouting] BOO!

clips.text: Tom! Get out here and look at my roses!
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, shouting from the street, indignant] Tom! [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, loud, aggrieved] Get out here and look at my ROSES!

clips.text: In my own kitchen! Tom, back at Rikers I had a key to every door in the place, and here I can't get near a muffin. You know, one time a fella tried to walk out of the mess hall with a whole loaf of bread under his hat...
clips.script: [thick New York accent, goofy outrage] In my own KITCHEN! [thick New York accent, chatty, building] Tom, back at Rikers I had a key to every door in the place, and here I can't get near a MUFFIN. [thick New York accent, settling into a story, relaxed] You know, one time a fella tried to walk out of the mess hall with a whole loaf of bread under his hat...

clips.text: Password accepted. Welcome, Agent...
clips.script: [tiny, formal] Password accepted. Welcome, Agent...

clips.text: Tom! My gumbo's been on since six, and right now it's the temperature of a handshake.
clips.script: [indignant, Creole warmth] Tom! [stern, aggrieved] My gumbo's been on since six, [flat, withering] and right now it's the temperature of a HANDSHAKE.

clips.text: That's my dog under the table, and I've never seen that loaf before in my life.
clips.script: [quick, innocent, sharp] That's my dog under the table, [deadpan, sweet] and I've never seen that loaf before in my LIFE.

clips.text: My griddle is cold. Do you know what a pupusa is off a cold griddle? It's an apology.
clips.script: [fierce, proud] My griddle is cold. [pointed, rhetorical] Do you know what a pupusa is off a cold griddle? [dry, devastating] It's an APOLOGY.

clips.text: Stop right there. Somebody's had a fire going in this building, and I'm putting an end to it.
clips.script: [stern, soggy, disapproving] Stop right there. [cold, officious] Somebody's had a fire going in this building, [self-righteous] and I'm putting an end to it.

clips.text: What's in the salad spinner? Is that sourdough? No. Too sour.
clips.script: [sniffy, fussy] What's in the salad spinner? [suspicious] Is that sourdough? [dismissive, curt] No. Too SOUR.

clips.text: No. Ours now.
clips.script: [thick, wet, flat] No. Ours now.

clips.text: "Bohemian Rye-psody!"
clips.script: [delighted, singing it out] "Bohemian... [proud of the pun] RYE-psody!"

clips.text: Bready Mercury was climbing out of the crock at five this morning. I wasn't going to argue with him.
clips.script: [mellow, easy] bready mercury was climbing out of the crock at five this morning. [mellow, laid-back, low-key, shrugging, unbothered] i wasn't going to argue with him.

clips.text: How big?
clips.script: [sharp, businesslike] How BIG?

clips.text: Fifty years I fed the night crews out of this room. Then one morning in 1963 they shut off my gas and chained the door, and not one of them said a word to me about it.
clips.script: [gruff, proud, old workman] Fifty years I fed the night crews out of this room. [flat, simmering] Then one morning in nineteen sixty-three they shut off my gas and chained the door, [bitter, indignant] and not one of them said a WORD to me about it.
